messages.author: 66537eeccf3193f3
messages.subject: Record genotypes
parts:
Hi, I am trying to clean up my snp data by filter out any alleles that have depth < 3 and if the total depth of the locus is < 5 then exclude the genotype altogether i.e. turn into NA. Then I tried to record the "clean" genotypes back into genlight object. This is where I stuck. 

# Recall genotypes based on the new depth filter
het <- Map(function(x, y) x>0 & y>0, read.depth.ref.filter, read.depth.snp.filter)
hom_0 <- Map(function(x, y) x>0 & y==0, read.depth.ref.filter, read.depth.snp.filter)
hom_2 <- Map(function(x, y) x==0 & y>0, read.depth.ref.filter, read.depth.snp.filter)

re.geno <- read.depth.snp.filter

# Record the genotype table
re.geno[] <- Map(ifelse, het, 1, re.geno)
re.geno[] <- Map(ifelse, hom_0, 0, re.geno)
re.geno[] <- Map(ifelse, hom_2, 2, re.geno)

gl[,] <- t(re.geno[,])  ### This is where I stuck. 

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. 

R.

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Record genotypes
parts:
Hi Sun,

Read depth cannot be calculated from the data and so must be either

(a) Calculated from the locus metadata provided by DArT (gl.read.dart does this) or
(b) Provided by the user at the time of transferring the data to dartR.

Given that you have read your data into dartR from a vcf file, you would need to obtain the read depth for each locus and then add it in to the locus metadata.

gl@other$loc.metrics$rdepth <- read.depth

Once you have done that, you can use gl.report.rdepth and gl.filter.rdepth to do the job.

Hope this helps.

Arthur

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Record genotypes
parts:
Hi Sun,

If you have already inserted the read depth for each allele at each locus then your best option I think is to create a new rdepth variable in the loc.metrics using one o

gl@other$loc.metrics$rdepth <- mean(rd.allele1,rd.allele2) OR
gl@other$loc.metrics$rdepth <- min(rd.allele1,rd.allele2) OR
gl@other$loc.metrics$rdepth <- max(rd.allele1,rd.allele2)  ## replace rd.allele with your names.

Your choice. Then use

gl <- gl.filter.rdepth(gl, lower=5, upper=50)

A

messages.author: f7c335e987e6a186
messages.subject: recreating RepAvg metric?
parts:
Hi folks,

I have a couple of DArT reports for targeted SNPs (that were previously shown to be highly variable for our target species). These reports have a different format to previous reports I've dealt with, and I'm not able to directly read them into dartR using gl.read.dart() because the RepAvg column was not provided. Instead I have the following columns:

MarkerName
AlleleType
AlleleSequence
CallRate
OneRatioRef
OneRatioSnp
FreqHomRef
FreqHomSnp
FreqHets
PICRef
PICSnp
AvgPIC
AvgCountRefRaw
AvgCountSnpRaw
sum
RatioAvgCountRefAvgCountSnpRaw
AvgCountRefNormFilt
AvgCountSnpNormFilt
RatioAvgCountRefAvgCountSnpNormFilt

There are two data files. One has the SNP genotypes in 2-row format (does not have the 'sum' column), and the other has (presumably) the read coverage for each Ref and SNP for each genotype. How can I recalculate the RepAvg metric from the info I have, or otherwise import this data into dartR for further analysis?

Thanks,
Peter

messages.author: d87216285ace7535
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] recreating RepAvg metric?
parts:
You can simply add a column, call it RepAvg and give them all the same
value (between 0 and 1). It's usually the last column before the data.
It's not something you can calculate, that number comes from DArT itself
based on how often repeated samples gave the same result.

Cheers
Peter

On Saturday, February 27, 2021 at 10:56:33 PM UTC+8 Sun wrote:
Hi, I am trying to clean up my snp data by filter out any alleles that have depth < 3 and if the total depth of the locus is < 5 then exclude the genotype altogether i.e. turn into NA. Then I tried to record the "clean" genotypes back into genlight object. This is where I stuck. 

# Recall genotypes based on the new depth filter
het <- Map(function(x, y) x>0 & y>0, read.depth.ref.filter, read.depth.snp.filter)
hom_0 <- Map(function(x, y) x>0 & y==0, read.depth.ref.filter, read.depth.snp.filter)
hom_2 <- Map(function(x, y) x==0 & y>0, read.depth.ref.filter, read.depth.snp.filter)

re.geno <- read.depth.snp.filter

# Record the genotype table
re.geno[] <- Map(ifelse, het, 1, re.geno)
re.geno[] <- Map(ifelse, hom_0, 0, re.geno)
re.geno[] <- Map(ifelse, hom_2, 2, re.geno)

gl[,] <- t(re.geno[,])  ### This is where I stuck. 

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. 

R.
